evidence: Inspected the actual draft body of def-scientific-statistical-model-contract. It explicitly distinguishes biological units from technical repeats of the same specimen, states that neither role implies independence, and requires the target, assignment unit, observation mechanism, and adequacy assumptions to be recorded. The local model uses those role distinctions and states its independence assumptions separately. This verifies the declared interface only; it does not claim batch-1 worker acceptance or gate approval.

Inspected the actual draft body of def-linear-mixed-model. It defines finite-dimensional Y=Xβ+Zb+ε with square-integrable mean-zero b and ε, their covariance matrices, and independence between b and ε; it imposes no Gaussian assumption and identifies subject/visit roles. The local model is the random-intercept special case and strengthens the component assumptions to mutual independence across biological effects and technical errors with common variances. The local variance proof does not rely on batch 7's marginal-covariance lemma. This verifies the declared interface only; it does not claim batch-7 worker acceptance or gate approval.

The actual supplier definition distinguishes a biological unit from a technical repeat of the same specimen and explicitly says those labels do not assert independence. The new definition preserves that convention and separately declares mutual independence as a model assumption; it also identifies the cluster receiving treatment as the randomization unit when assignment occurs at cluster level.

The actual supplier definition states the moment-only finite-dimensional model Y=Xβ+Zb+ε, E[b]=E[ε]=0, Cov(b)=G, Cov(ε)=R, and b independent of ε, with subject/visit indexing and no Gaussianity. The local item specializes the fixed mean by unit and a random intercept B_i, then adds the stronger mutual-independence and common-variance hypotheses needed by its balanced-mean theorem.
